subject: Media Literacy
title: Reading Critically: A Practical Framework
description: A 60-second lesson on Reading Critically: A Practical Framework.

hook.text: A media professor reads three articles about the same event in under five minutes and identifies all three biases.

buildup.text: Critical reading involves checking the source, identifying the frame, noting who's quoted, and spotting what's missing.

discovery.text: The five key questions: Who wrote it? Who published it? Who benefits? What's missing? What's the frame?

twist.text: These questions take 30 seconds but most people never ask them. We consume news on autopilot.

climax.text: Critical reading isn't skepticism about everything. It's informed engagement with the choices behind every story.

punchline.text: Five questions. Thirty seconds. A completely different understanding.

quiz.question: Which is NOT one of the five critical reading questions?
